## My thinking

I've been farming three years now, so I mostly follow what the experienced farmers around me do in Quzhou. My land is 340.1 mu and my main system is the winter wheat–summer maize rotation — that's what makes sense here on the North China Plain. I'll put 220 mu into that rotation because it gives me two harvests on the same ground every year. The other 120 mu I'll split evenly: 60 mu for oilseed (peanut, which does well here) and 60 mu for soybean.

For wheat I use improved varieties — the local seed station recommends them and they're what everyone uses. For maize I go hybrid, no question, the yield difference is obvious. For peanut and soybean I use improved, nothing fancy.

I have well irrigation, which is the only reason I can grow reliably in this dry climate. Wheat needs at least three waterings — before sowing, at jointing, and at heading. Maize I direct-seed right after wheat harvest, no-till, so I save time. It needs two irrigations around tasseling and grain fill.

Fertilizer: I follow what the neighbors do, maybe slightly on the higher end for wheat since that's my main cash crop. Peanut and soybean fix nitrogen themselves so I barely apply N there, mainly phosphorus and potassium.
